clue.text: Enthusiastic head touring second small Scottish island

indicators.note: a head touring something goes all the way round it, so the other pieces sit inside

parts.note: pate is an old word for the head
S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
Iona is an island in the Inner Hebrides

explanation.surface: An eager leader goes round a second, smaller island off Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' looks like a leader but is the old word for the top of the skull; Iona is a small island in the Inner Hebrides.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone passionate about a thing is full of zeal for it, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Bouquet from Percy's opponent turned up

indicators.note: turned up says the hidden letters are read backwards
from here says the letters are taken out of the words that follow, lying within them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Flowers from Harry Percy's rival, overturned.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft lacked an indicator for the hiding; 'from' supplies it. In a down clue 'turned up' reads the letters bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: A posy is a small bunch of flowers, a little bouquet.

clue.text: Little study in support of first course?

indicators.note: in a down clue a support sits underneath, so this piece goes below

parts.note: soup is often the first course of a meal
to con is to study or learn by heart

explanation.surface: A short reading backing the starter at dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little' is a noun here, a trace, as in a soupcon of garlic.
explanation.definitionFit: A soupcon is a tiny amount or hint of something, a little bit.

clue.text: Old collectors from both sides parting in eastern location

indicators.note: parting means splitting apart, so these letters go inside the other piece

parts.note: a venue is a location
both sides are left and right, L AND R

explanation.surface: Former tax men from left and right at an eastern venue.
explanation.walkthrough: The Inland Revenue was the UK's tax collecting department until it merged into HMRC in 2005.
explanation.definitionFit: The former British tax authority gathered taxes, so it was a body of collectors, now gone.

clue.text: One showing barefaced cheek?

parts.note: cheek means bottom here, and someone who shows a bare one without shame is a nudist

explanation.definitionFit: A naturist practises nudism, so bare buttocks are on show, not just a bold attitude.

clue.text: Flower material

definitions.meaning: a flower is something that flows, a river

explanation.definitionFit: The Tweed is a Scottish river, and tweed is also the woollen fabric for jackets.

clue.text: Piece of music inspired by Jolson grates

indicators.note: a thing inspired by others is drawn from within them, so the letters are taken from inside these words

explanation.surface: A tune that came to mind because Al Jolson's voice grated.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across the end of Jolson into the start of grates.
explanation.definitionFit: A song is a short composition for singing, one kind of musical piece.

clue.text: Something blown in old vehicle auntie regularly turned over

parts.note: a car is a vehicle

indicators.note: turned over means flipped round, so these letters are read in reverse
regularly means every other letter is taken

explanation.surface: Something exploding in an old car that an aunt kept overturning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' picks ANI from auntie, which 'turned over' reverses to INA.
explanation.definitionFit: An ocarina is a small egg-shaped wind instrument, played by blowing.

clue.text: Not so fine, maybe, without foundation?

definitions.meaning: coffee ... is not ground so fine, coarser
without basis, and ground is literally a foundation

explanation.definitionFit: Groundless claims lack any basis, while read as two words it describes coarser grinding.

clue.text: Row headcase reported

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by word of mouth, so the word is the one heard

parts.note: the skull is literally the case round the head

explanation.surface: An argument with a lunatic got reported in the news.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Headcase' looks like slang for a madman, but it is read literally as the bony case of the head.
explanation.definitionFit: To scull is to propel a boat with oars, so it is a way to row.

clue.text: Strangely, Mike had to work on stage

indicators.note: letters arranged strangely are put in an unexpected new order

explanation.surface: Oddly, Mike was obliged to do some acting in the theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'work on stage' reads like acting, but it is a stage work: The Mikado is the Gilbert and Sullivan comic opera.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mikado is a comic opera, a theatrical work performed in front of an audience.

clue.text: Drunken son overcome by home brew scoffed, being selfish

parts.note: in means at home

indicators.note: something overcome by another is engulfed by it, so it goes inside

parts.note: cider is a brewed drink

indicators.note: drunken letters stagger into a new order

parts.note: to scoff is to eat greedily, so scoffed means ate

explanation.surface: A drunk son, floored by home-made brew he has guzzled, behaves thoughtlessly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drunken' is the anagram signal on son, and 'overcome by' sets the result inside the brew, splitting it after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Inconsiderate people ignore others' feelings, thinking only of themselves.

clue.text: Clash with prisoner caught during convention

parts.note: con is short for convict, a prisoner

indicators.note: something happening during another is contained within its span

parts.note: a convention is an established custom, a tradition
C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A dispute in which a convict was nabbed at a conference.
explanation.walkthrough: 'convention' suggests a conference, but here it means a custom.
explanation.definitionFit: A contradiction is a conflict between two statements or facts, so they clash.

clue.text: Few peers on occasion will stop chorusing nonsense?

indicators.note: a piece that stops another plugs it, sitting inside

parts.note: scatting is singing nonsense syllables, as in jazz scat

indicators.note: on occasion means only now and then, so alternate letters are taken

explanation.surface: A handful of lords will now and then halt a choir singing gibberish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on occasion' picks ER from peers.
explanation.definitionFit: A scattering is a small, sparse number, as in a scattering of guests.

clue.text: Moderate unusually strict over backing North-East

indicators.note: over here means spread over and around the other piece, enclosing it
letters arranged unusually are not in their normal order
backing means going in reverse, so these letters run backwards

parts.note: NE is the compass abbreviation for north-east

explanation.surface: A mild sort is unexpectedly harsh about supporting the north-east of England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusually' shuffles strict, 'backing' turns the compass pair round, and 'over' wraps the shuffled letters around it after their first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A centrist holds middle-of-the-road political views, the noun sense of a moderate.

clue.text: At one point almost everyone is available if required

indicators.note: almost the word means all of it bar the final letter

parts.note: once means at one point in time
all means everyone

explanation.surface: Once upon a time, nearly all of us were there when needed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops the last letter of ONCE.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctor on call can be summoned at any moment, ready to work if needed.

clue.text: Jurgen maybe unveiled team with Alexander-Arnold ultimately lacking balance

indicators.note: unveiled means uncovered, stripped of its outside letters

parts.note: Jurgen Klopp was Liverpool's football manager
a side is a team

indicators.note: ultimately means at the very end, so the last letter

explanation.surface: Jurgen Klopp unveils a lineup that is off balance once Trent Alexander-Arnold is missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unveiled' strips K and P from KLOPP; Trent Alexander-Arnold played for Liverpool under him.
explanation.definitionFit: Something lopsided is uneven, with more weight on one side than the other.

clue.text: Do well from article covering privy with no walls

indicators.note: a cover wraps round what it covers, so the other letters sit inside

parts.note: the is the definite article

indicators.note: without its walls the word loses its outside letters, leaving the middle

explanation.surface: Making a success out of a newspaper piece about a toilet without walls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no walls' strips the outer letters of privy to leave RIV.
explanation.definitionFit: To thrive is to flourish or prosper, which is doing well.

clue.text: Negotiate again somewhere quiet?

definitions.meaning: to ... is to treat, or negotiate, again
a peaceful place to withdraw to

explanation.definitionFit: Read as re-treat it means to bargain once more; as one word it is a secluded haven.

clue.text: Talk about men with sick animals

indicators.note: one piece goes about another, enclosing it

parts.note: to gas is to talk idly at length
OR, other ranks, means ordinary soldiers, men
ill means sick

explanation.surface: A chat about some men and their diseased livestock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Talk about men' tempts a homophone of guerrillas, but the clue is a charade inside GAS.
explanation.definitionFit: Gorillas are great apes, a particular kind of animal.

clue.text: Hotels rebuilt round country

indicators.note: rebuilt means put together again in a different form

parts.note: O is round in shape

explanation.surface: Hotels being reconstructed all over a nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rebuilt' rearranges HOTELS into LESOTH.
explanation.definitionFit: Lesotho is a small kingdom in southern Africa, a nation.

clue.text: One inside messaging officials — not initially, they might put a dampener on things

definitions.text: they might put a dampener on things

indicators.note: not initially means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: texting is messaging by phone

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: ushers are officials who show people to seats
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A person among some texting officials is a killjoy, it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not initially' applies only to messaging; 'inside' sets the numeral one within the officials, who are people showing guests to seats.
explanation.definitionFit: Fire extinguishers spray water or foam, literally damping down whatever is burning.

clue.text: Inappropriate fun a drug user has in prime positions

indicators.note: only the letters standing at prime-numbered places in the phrase are kept, the rest being thrown out

explanation.surface: It's improper for a drug taker to be having fun in top jobs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prime positions' sounds like top spots, but keeps letters 2, 3, 5, 7 and 11 of 'fun a drug user', discarding F, A, R, G, U, S, R.
explanation.definitionFit: Undue means excessive or unwarranted, beyond what is fitting.

clue.text: Genuine end to hostilities when Conservative leaves

indicators.note: a letter that leaves a word is taken out of it

parts.note: a truce ends fighting

explanation.surface: A real ceasefire comes when the Tory walks out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end to hostilities' suggests the last letter of a word, but it is a truce.
explanation.definitionFit: True and genuine are synonyms, meaning real or authentic.

clue.text: Crikey, it wasn't me!

definitions.meaning: An exclamation of surprise, like crikey

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase works both as an amazed exclamation and as a denial of having done something.

clue.text: Page leaving previous Queen's bloomers? Just one

indicators.note: a letter leaving a word is taken out of it

parts.note: past means previous
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: A page boy leaves with the late Queen's underwear, just one pair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomers' suggests knickers, but means flowers; just one gives a single flower.
explanation.definitionFit: An aster is a daisy-like garden flower, a single plant that blooms.

clue.text: With this entrance, our dancing could result in outrage

indicators.note: letters dancing move about into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Our dancing at this doorway could cause public anger.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer plus OUR, shuffled together ('dancing'), make OUTRAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A gate is a way in through a fence or wall, so an entrance.

clue.text: Interfering in demos, led astray by this writer

indicators.note: letters led astray wander from their proper order

parts.note: this writer means the setter, me

explanation.surface: A meddler at protests, misled by the person writing this.
explanation.walkthrough: 'astray' rearranges DEMOS and LED into MEDDLESO.
explanation.definitionFit: A meddlesome person pokes into others' business, constantly butting in.
